title: Treesa-Gayatri Secure Historic World Championships Bronze
indian_angle: This marks India's continued success in women's doubles and is a significant achievement at the World Championships.
summary: Indian duo Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand secured a bronze medal at the BWF World Championships after their semi-final defeat, marking a historic achievement for Indian women's doubles badminton.

title: Gopichand Outlines India's Asian Games Strategy Post-Worlds
indian_angle: Coach Pullela Gopichand's plans are crucial for India's medal prospects at the upcoming Asian Games, building on recent World Championships success.
summary: Following the BWF World Championships, national coach Pullela Gopichand detailed India's focused training strategy for the Asian Games, aiming to achieve targets one step at a time.

title: Treesa-Gayatri Proud of Bronze, See It As Just The Start
indian_angle: The young Indian pair expresses pride in their historic World Championships bronze, signaling their ambition for future successes.
summary: Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand expressed pride in their historic World Championships bronze medal, viewing it as a significant milestone and just the beginning of their journey in international badminton.

title: Satwik-Chirag Exit World Championships in Quarter-Finals
indian_angle: India's top men's doubles pair, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, faced a challenging exit from the World Championships.
summary: Indian men's doubles pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty were defeated by China's Chang and Liang in the BWF World Championships quarter-finals, bowing out 21-18, 21-9.

title: Treesa-Gayatri End 15-Year Wait for Women's Doubles World Medal
indian_angle: This thrilling quarter-final victory secured India's first women's doubles World Championships medal in 15 years, a historic moment for the nation.
summary: Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand stunned Chinese fourth seeds Jia and Zhang with a 16-21, 21-15, 21-13 victory in the quarter-finals, securing India's first women's doubles World Championships medal in 15 years.

title: Indian Junior Coaching Camp for Asia U17 & U15 Championships
indian_angle: This coaching camp in Guwahati is vital for preparing India's young talent for the upcoming Badminton Asia U17 & U15 Junior Championships.
summary: An Indian team coaching camp is underway at the National Center of Excellence in Guwahati for the Badminton Asia U17 & U15 Junior Championships 2026, focusing on developing junior talent.
